domain.name: GDP
domain.description: Global Data Platform conformed model: customers, accounts and sales hierarchies shared across business units.

targets.description: Conformed customer dimension. Current state of every customer known to the systems of record.

columns.name: CUSTOMER_KEY
columns.definition: Surrogate key: MD5 hash of the business key customer_id.

columns.name: CUSTOMER_ID
columns.definition: Enterprise customer identifier supplied by the CRM system of record.

columns.name: CUSTOMER_NAME
columns.definition: Customer full name, trimmed and title-cased.

columns.name: CUSTOMER_STATUS
columns.definition: Lifecycle status of the customer relationship.

columns.name: SALES_REGION
columns.definition: Sales region responsible for the customer.

columns.name: EMAIL_ADDRESS
columns.definition: Primary email address of the customer, lower-cased.

columns.name: CUSTOMER_CREATED_DATE
columns.definition: Date the customer was first created in the system of record.

columns.name: RECORD_SOURCE
columns.definition: Source system the row was loaded from.

columns.name: LOADED_AT
columns.definition: Timestamp at which dbt loaded the row.

knowledge.title: Customer identifier
knowledge.content: The enterprise customer identifier. CRM extracts call it cust_no, cust_id or customer_number. Maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID and is the business key of the customer dimension.

knowledge.title: Customer name
knowledge.content: Full name of the customer. Source systems use cust_nm, cust_name or full_name. Maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_NAME.

knowledge.title: Birth date
knowledge.content: Customer date of birth, abbreviated dob or birth_dt in source systems. Personal data; maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.BIRTH_DATE.

knowledge.title: Customer status
knowledge.content: Lifecycle status of the customer relationship. Sources send single-letter codes in a status or cust_status column. Maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_STATUS.

knowledge.title: Sales region
knowledge.content: Sales region that owns the customer. Sources call it region or sales_rgn. Maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.SALES_REGION.

knowledge.title: Email address
knowledge.content: Primary email of the customer. Personal data. Maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.EMAIL_ADDRESS.

knowledge.title: Customer created date
knowledge.content: Date the customer record was created in the source CRM (created_date, create_dt). Maps to DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_CREATED_DATE.

knowledge.title: Customer status code decode
knowledge.content: CRM status codes decode to GDP customer status: A = ACTIVE, I = INACTIVE, P = PROSPECT. Unknown codes are not allowed in the dimension.

knowledge.title: Sales region standardisation
knowledge.content: Region values are trimmed and upper-cased before loading. Allowed regions: NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST, CENTRAL.

knowledge.title: Person names
knowledge.content: Person names are trimmed and title-cased with the approved initcap_trim macro. When the source splits given and family name (FIRST_NM / LAST_NM), concatenate them.

knowledge.title: Full name from first and last
knowledge.content: CRM extracts that store FIRST_NM and LAST_NM separately are concatenated, trimmed and title-cased into CUSTOMER_NAME.

knowledge.title: Email addresses
knowledge.content: Email addresses are trimmed and lower-cased.

knowledge.title: Dates delivered as text
knowledge.content: Dates delivered as MM/DD/YYYY text are parsed with TRY_TO_DATE so malformed values become NULL instead of failing the load.

knowledge.title: GDP naming standard
knowledge.content: Columns are upper snake case in Snowflake and lower snake case in dbt. Identifiers end in _ID, surrogate keys in _KEY, dates in _DATE, timestamps in _AT or _TS. Models: stg_<source>__<table>, int_<entity>__<verb>, dim_<entity>, fct_<process>.

knowledge.title: GDP datatype standard
knowledge.content: Identifiers are VARCHAR. Dates are DATE, event times TIMESTAMP_NTZ in UTC. Amounts NUMBER(18,2). Codes are decoded to readable values in conformed dimensions.

knowledge.title: DIM_CUSTOMER model
knowledge.content: DIM_CUSTOMER is the conformed customer dimension at grain one row per customer_id. Type 1 slowly changing: attributes are overwritten with the latest CRM values. Duplicate source rows are resolved by keeping the most recently created record.

knowledge.title: STTM table design for dimensions
knowledge.content: Every dimension STTM states grain, business keys, deduplication rule, SCD type and incremental strategy. Type 1 dimensions use an incremental merge on the business key. Surrogate keys are MD5 of the business key; RECORD_SOURCE and LOADED_AT are platform-derived.

knowledge.title: GDP dbt layering
knowledge.content: Staging models select from sources, rename to lower snake case and cast nothing. Intermediate models deduplicate. Mart models apply STTM transformations, cast to target types and are incremental merges for dimensions.

knowledge.title: Soda checks for dimensions
knowledge.content: Write official SodaCL. Dimensions must have row_count > 0, missing_count and duplicate_count = 0 on the business key, missing_count = 0 on required columns, invalid_count with valid values for codes, valid format email as a warning, freshness(loaded_at) < 1d as a warning, and a schema fail when required columns are missing.

knowledge.title: Approved mapping CUST_ID to CUSTOMER_ID
knowledge.content: Previous CRM onboarding: CRM_CUSTOMER.CUST_ID was approved as DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID (enterprise identifier).

knowledge.title: Approved mapping CUSTOMER_NM to CUSTOMER_NAME
knowledge.content: Previous CRM onboarding: CUSTOMER_NM was approved as DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_NAME with INITCAP(TRIM()).

knowledge.title: Approved mapping BIRTH_DT to BIRTH_DATE
knowledge.content: Previous CRM onboarding: BIRTH_DT was approved as DIM_CUSTOMER.BIRTH_DATE.

knowledge.title: Approved mapping CUST_STATUS to CUSTOMER_STATUS
knowledge.content: Previous CRM onboarding: CUST_STATUS codes were approved as DIM_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_STATUS using the status decode rule.

knowledge.title: Unparseable birth dates
knowledge.content: Birth dates that cannot be parsed load as NULL; Soda reports them as a warning rather than failing the load.

knowledge.title: Onboarding a Snowflake share
knowledge.content: An admin mounts the share with CREATE DATABASE ... FROM SHARE and grants IMPORTED PRIVILEGES to the platform role. Register the mounted database as SNOWFLAKE_SHARE, select tables, validate access, then land as-is with CTAS and reconcile row counts.
